pick.headline: Iran breaks relations with Britain over Rushdie
pick.summary: On March 7, 1989, Iran broke diplomatic relations with Britain over London's refusal to act against Salman Rushdie and The Satanic Verses.
pick.significance: Relations were not fully restored until 1999, when Iran's government distanced itself from the death decree.
pick.fbis: The Near East & South Asia Daily Report of March 7, 1989, opened its review with IRNA citing Iran's Foreign Ministry on the "complete severance of diplomatic ties with Britain" for failing to meet the Majlis conditions over Salman Rushdie's novel.

evidence.title: FBIS Daily Report: Near East & South Asia, No. 043, 7 March 1989
evidence.snippet: FBIS-NES-89-043 7 March 1989 7 March Middle East and South Asia Review LD0703144389 [Editorial Report] The Foreign Ministry announced the “complete sever- ance of diplomatic ties with Britain” for its failure to fulfill the conditions set by the Majlis to clarity its position on the Salman Rushdie novel, IRNA reported, citing a 7 March statement issued by the ministry.
